subject: fit indices for a cfa based on 2 groups/samples

messages.author: 4dbe946c78d7e634
messages.subject: fit indices for a cfa based on 2 groups/samples
parts:
Hi,

I have a question regarding fit indices for a cfa based on 2
groups/samples. Specifically, I have fitted a cfa model with one
factor based on 7 indicators (questionnaire items), and two samples
(clinical vs. non-clinical), with the restriction of equal factor
loadings in both samples, using the following code:

fit <- cfa (Model, data = data, group = sample, group.equal = c("loadings"))

The summary of fit measures provides me with two different chi-square
values for the two samples, but only one value for supplemental fit
measures including the RMSEA, SRMR, CFI, TLI.

My question being, is it not possible to get supplemental fit measures
for both samples? And what do supplemental fit measures in the output
refer to? My understanding was that supplemental fit indices (RMSEA,
CFI....) are ultimately based on the chi-square and I am struggling to
understand why there are separate chi-square values by (sub-)sample
and just one value for the entire sample for the supplemental fit
indices. Is there a way to get either an individual chi-square value
for the whole sample, or supplemental fit indices by group?

--

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: fit indices for a cfa based on 2 groups/samples
parts: The summary of fit measures provides me with two different chi-square values for the two samples

No, those are each group's contribution to the chi-squared statistic.  If you made no equality constraints across groups (configural invariance), then those contributions would be equivalent to the individual chi-squared statistics from separate 1-group models fit to each sample.  But when you have equality constraints across groups, that will not be the case: each group has some influence over parameters that apply to them both, so the chi-squared contributions (and associated degrees of freedom) are not independent.
what do supplemental fit measures in the output refer to?
Overall (mis)fit of the model to both groups, simultaneously.
Is there a way to get either an individual chi-square value for the whole sample
Yes, that is the line at the top of the summary() output, labeled "Model Fit Test Statistic" (with its df and p value below it).
or supplemental fit indices by group?

No, not when there are constraints across groups, because you cannot simply divide the df in half between the groups.  (Some df were obtained by constraining loadings across groups.)
